title: Pro Shop Store Credit: dormant-balance expiration basis
content:
## Basis
A Pro Shop Store Credit account's balance is forfeited for inactivity once the present moment is not before a set point in time: the account's own opened date — understood as the date the account was opened, or the date of its most recent top-up or redemption, whichever falls later — plus the tier's own inactivity period before expiration, counted in calendar days.

## Evidentiary basis
- The point in time this policy measures from is the account's own recorded opened date as held in the account's own system record; where a top-up or redemption has posted more recently than the opened date, that later date is what the clock runs from instead.
- The duration added to that point is the tier's own inactivity period before expiration, drawn from the tier the account holds.
- The days are counted as full calendar days, with no rounding for a partial day.
- "Not before" includes the boundary day itself: the moment the present instant reaches that point in time exactly, the balance is already subject to forfeiture; it need not have passed beyond it.

## Boundary cases
Suppose a tier's inactivity period before expiration is 180 days and the account's most recent qualifying date (opened, topped up, or redeemed from) was day 0.
- On day 179 since that date, the present moment is still before the anchor plus duration, so the balance is not yet forfeited.
- On day 180 since that date, the present moment is exactly at the anchor plus duration; because the boundary is inclusive, the balance is now subject to forfeiture for inactivity.

## Points of judgement
Any top-up or redemption posted after the account was opened resets the point this policy measures from to that later transaction's own date; only the absence of any top-up or redemption newer than the opened date leaves the opened date itself as the measuring point.
